sc_pop_quiz.text: The teacher announces a pop quiz. You did the reading for roughly one of the three chapters.

outcomes.lucky: Your confident guessing pays off. You are now suspicious of how easy that was.
outcomes.flop: Confidence did not make the answers correct. The teacher writes 'interesting' next to three of them.

sc_cheat_exam.text: The exam is hard. The kid next to you has a clear view of every answer and the posture of someone who studied.

outcomes.got_away: You copy flawlessly. Your grade rises and your conscience sends a polite email.
outcomes.caught: The teacher is standing behind you. She says nothing, which is worse, then takes your paper.

sc_science_fair.text: The science fair is next week. Your project idea is either brilliant or a baking soda volcano.

outcomes.win: Your project wins a ribbon. You hold it in the car like it's a fragile animal.
outcomes.meltdown: The device smokes, then stops. A judge nods kindly and writes 'effort'.

sc_bully_lunch.text: A larger kid has decided your lunch is his lunch. This is the third day running.

outcomes.respect: He blinks, shrugs, and leaves. You eat your sandwich shaking, but you eat it.
outcomes.bruised: It does not go well. Your sandwich, however, survives. Small mercies.

sc_school_play.text: Auditions are open for the school play. There are many trees available and one lead.

outcomes.lead: You get the lead. Your family attends with a banner and a concerning amount of flowers.
outcomes.tree: You are cast as Tree Number Three. You commit to the role deeply.

sc_field_trip.text: The class field trip is to a museum of old machinery. The permission slip needs a signature by tomorrow.

outcomes.found: You find a room nobody else did. It has a giant gear. You consider it yours.
outcomes.lost: You get lost near the gift shop. A guard escorts you back like a minor celebrity.

sc_favorite_teacher.text: A teacher takes a real interest in you. They hand you a book and say, 'You might like this.'

sc_strict_teacher.text: Your new teacher runs the class like a small, tidy dictatorship. Today's rule concerns pencils.

outcomes.respect: She considers it, nods, and amends the rule. You feel like a diplomat.
outcomes.detention: She considers it, nods, and adds your name to a list.

sc_homework_dog.text: You didn't do your homework. The classic excuse is right there, waiting.

outcomes.bought: The teacher, who has heard this for years, grants you an extension out of sheer respect.
outcomes.denied: You don't own a dog. The teacher knows this. She has your file.

sc_detention_prank.text: Your friends dare you to put a rubber duck in the principal's chair. It seems statistically safe.

outcomes.legend: The principal sits, squeaks, and looks directly at nobody. You are a quiet legend.
outcomes.suspended: There are cameras. You are suspended for three days and the duck is confiscated.

sc_spelling_bee.text: You've reached the final round of the spelling bee. The word is 'necessary'. It has two rivals inside it.

outcomes.right: You nail it. The crowd claps. A teacher dabs at her eye with a tissue.
outcomes.wrong: You add an extra 's'. The bell sounds like a verdict.

sc_group_project.text: You're assigned a group project with three classmates. One of them is already asleep.

outcomes.works: Everyone does their part, which is rare enough to deserve a plaque.
outcomes.fails: Two of them 'forgot'. You present alone and sweat politely.

sc_final_exams.text: Finals week arrives. Your desk is covered in notes, snacks, and denial.

outcomes.pass: You pass on caffeine and fear. Your hands shake, but the numbers are good.
outcomes.blank: You fall asleep during the exam. The proctor lets you finish drooling.

sc_skip_class.text: It's a sunny day and you're about to be in a math lesson. The back door of the building is unlocked.

outcomes.free: You spend the day at the park. It is an excellent day with no consequences.
outcomes.caught: A teacher spots you by the fountain. Your parents receive a very formal phone call.

sc_sports_tryout.text: The school teams are holding tryouts. You have the build of a person who owns many good books.

outcomes.made: You make the team. Your coach calls you 'scrappy' and means it kindly.
outcomes.cut: You are cut by lunch. You get a free orange slice for your trouble.

sc_cafeteria_dare.text: Someone dares you to eat a mystery lunch special in one go. The crowd forms like a flock of gulls.

outcomes.champ: You finish. The cafeteria erupts. You will taste it for a week.
outcomes.sick: You return it dramatically in the hallway. The nurse suspends you for 'general reasons'.

sc_standardized_test.text: The big standardized test is on Saturday. Your future is apparently a bubble sheet.

outcomes.good: The test goes surprisingly well. You attribute it to rest and charm.
outcomes.bad: The test goes about as well as you'd expect from a nap.

sc_class_clown.text: You have a joke ready that is either legendary or career-ending. The class is quiet. The teacher is turned around.

outcomes.laugh: The room explodes. You are briefly the funniest person alive.
outcomes.silence: A single cough. The teacher turns around. You assign yourself a grade of F.

sc_new_kid.text: A new kid joins your class and sits alone at lunch, holding a lunchbox like a shield.

sc_study_group.text: A friend suggests a study group. It will either be productive or a pizza discussion with textbooks nearby.

un_roommate_mess.text: Your roommate's side of the room has become a geological feature. A bowl of something has achieved sentience.

outcomes.clean: Your roommate apologizes and cleans for an afternoon. The bowl is given a funeral.
outcomes.fight: The talk becomes a fight about a borrowed charger. Both of you sleep poorly.

un_all_nighter.text: You have a paper due at nine. It is currently midnight and the paper is a title.

outcomes.pass: You write the paper in a fugue state. It's good. You don't remember writing it.
outcomes.flop: You turn in a paper that ends mid-sentence, which a professor might call a bold choice.

un_frat_party.text: A fraternity throws an enormous party. The invitation is a person yelling it at you on the lawn.

outcomes.fun: You have a wonderful time and meet three people who will remember you as 'the dancer'.
outcomes.rough: The night ends with a sticky floor, a lost jacket, and a mild existential question.

un_midterm.text: Midterms are upon you. The library is full of people whispering their problems to textbooks.

outcomes.curve: The class average is so bad that you feel brilliant by comparison.
outcomes.no_curve: The professor does not believe in curves. The grade is perfectly circular.

un_student_loan.text: Your loan paperwork arrives. The number at the bottom is large enough to have its own gravity.

un_prof_office_hours.text: A professor invites you to office hours. The sign says 'knock', which feels like both a request and a warning.

un_change_major.text: You aren't sure your major is right for you. You aren't sure of much, which is fairly normal at nineteen.

outcomes.better: The new major fits like a good jacket. You wonder why you waited.
outcomes.worse: The new major has extra requirements and a stranger's textbook. You carry on anyway.

un_dining_hall.text: The dining hall serves a casserole that may be pasta. Everyone is pretending it's fine.

outcomes.fine: It was surprisingly edible. You have the aura of a person who took a risk.
outcomes.sick: It was not edible. You get acquainted with the dorm bathroom.

un_plagiarism.text: A friend sends you a paper from last year. 'Just change a few words,' he says. The deadline is in three hours.

outcomes.pass: Nobody notices. You feel faintly like a smuggler.
outcomes.flagged: The software flags it in under a minute. The dean's email begins with 'Concerned'.

un_thesis.text: Your thesis advisor asks for 'a more compelling thesis'. Your thesis is a very compelling sentence about nothing.

outcomes.pass: The advisor approves. You are not sure why, which is common in academia.
outcomes.reject: The advisor suggests you 'start over, but sooner'.

un_study_abroad.text: Your school offers a semester abroad. The brochure shows people laughing near a canal.

outcomes.magic: You return with a better accent, worse sleep habits, and one perfect memory of bread.
outcomes.homesick: You spend a month homesick and two enjoying it. Overall, still worth it.

un_dorm_fire_alarm.text: The fire alarm goes off at 3 a.m. for the fourth time this month. The whole dorm stands outside in pajamas.

outcomes.fine: It was burnt popcorn. You are right and slightly smug.
outcomes.fined: The marshal finds you in bed and writes you a fine.

un_part_time_job.text: Your bank account is thin as a lecture handout. A campus job posting offers $12 an hour and free coffee.

un_dropout_thought.text: You stare at your bank statement, your syllabus, and your reflection. A voice suggests dropping out.

un_honors_offer.text: The honors program offers you a spot. It comes with extra work, extra pride, and extra sleeplessness.

wk_bad_boss.text: Your boss sends a three-line email that begins 'Per my last message' and ends in dread.

outcomes.respect: Your boss, caught off guard, softens. A rare sunbeam.
outcomes.grudge: Your boss suddenly takes an interest in your every move. You feel observed.

wk_promotion_offer.text: Your manager calls you in. A promotion is on the table, with more pay and slightly more fluorescent lighting.

outcomes.win: You negotiate well. The raise is bigger and the title includes the word 'Senior'.
outcomes.offended: Your manager sighs and offers a tiny raise. The promotion is mysteriously 'under review'.

wk_office_romance.text: A coworker keeps stopping by your desk with questions that feel suspiciously like not-work.

outcomes.sweet: They say yes. You share a quiet lunch and a slightly forbidden smile.
outcomes.awkward: They say no, politely. You both avoid the printer for a month.

wk_layoff_rumor.text: Rumors of layoffs spread by the break room. Your name is mentioned, then lowered, then mentioned again.

outcomes.safe: You prove yourself indispensable, or at least visible. The list passes you by.
outcomes.fired: The meeting is short. A box is provided. Your plant is returned to you.

wk_overtime.text: A project is behind schedule. Your manager asks, with practiced warmth, for a few extra hours.

outcomes.deal: Your manager agrees, nobly. You get a Friday afternoon back.
outcomes.no_deal: Your manager says 'we'll see.' Nobody sees.

wk_coworker_drama.text: Two coworkers aren't speaking. Each has asked you to carry messages with the gravity of diplomats.

outcomes.peace: They reconcile after a tense, very polite coffee. You are briefly the office hero.
outcomes.worse: Both now blame you. You are a diplomat with no embassy.

wk_union_vote.text: A union drive is underway. Posters appear in the break room. So do management's carefully worded emails.

wk_work_injury.text: You tweak your back lifting a box that was labeled 'light'. It was not light.

outcomes.fine: You walk it off. Your back writes a strongly worded letter for later.
outcomes.worse: It gets worse. A week in a heating-pad pose later, you reconsider heroism.

wk_whistleblow.text: You notice the company is quietly dumping something it shouldn't, in a place it shouldn't. Nobody else seems to see it.

outcomes.hero: Investigators act. You are quietly rewarded and loudly shunned.
outcomes.retaliation: You are fired 'for performance reasons' three days later. The timing is a coincidence, they say.

wk_fudge_numbers.text: Your manager asks you to 'smooth out' a quarterly report so the numbers look better than they are.

outcomes.rewarded: The numbers look lovely. Nobody checks. You check your own conscience and it shrugs.
outcomes.caught: An audit finds the discrepancy. You are fired with the polite speed of a trapdoor.

wk_microwave_fish.text: Someone microwaves fish in the office kitchen. The smell has taken hostages.

wk_team_building.text: Mandatory team-building: a trust fall, a trust sandwich, and a facilitator named Kyle who believes in all of it.

wk_stolen_lunch.text: Your lunch has vanished from the office fridge again. The label said 'Not for you'.

outcomes.gotcha: Your boss turns out to be the culprit and visibly sweats. You say nothing, delighted.
outcomes.backfire: The thief enjoys the spice. Your decoy was a gift.

wk_raise_ask.text: It's been a while since your last raise. You rehearse a speech in the bathroom mirror.

outcomes.yes: Your boss agrees. You say thank you six times and then leave before it changes.
outcomes.no: Your boss says the budget is 'tight' and then books a trip.

wk_headhunter.text: A recruiter emails you about 'an exciting opportunity'. The email has three emoji and no actual job title.

outcomes.offer: They offer much more money and a slightly unhinged mission statement. You take a day to think.
outcomes.nothing: The interview goes fine and nothing happens. A classic.

wk_credit_stealer.text: A coworker presents your idea in a meeting as their own, with a flourish you'd call 'artistic'.

outcomes.vindicated: You gently reclaim your idea. Everyone nods and several people take notes.
outcomes.awkward: The moment turns awkward and your coworker plays wounded. You lose a round.

wk_late_again.text: You wake up, look at the clock, and say a word you don't repeat at work. You're very late.

outcomes.believed: Your boss nods. Traffic is a universal truth.
outcomes.called_out: Your boss saw you in the parking lot ten minutes earlier.

wk_work_party.text: The holiday party features an open bar, a mediocre playlist, and your manager attempting a dance.

outcomes.legend: You become an office legend and nobody mentions it afterward.
outcomes.regret: You tell your boss exactly what you think of the stapler policy.

wk_new_hire.text: A new hire joins your team and stares at the coffee machine as if it's a puzzle.

wk_burnout.text: You catch yourself crying slightly at a spreadsheet. This feels like information.

outcomes.fine: The feeling passes. You wouldn't call it healed, but it moved.
outcomes.crash: You crash hard at your desk. A coworker brings you tea and says nothing, thankfully.

wk_presentation.text: You're asked to give a presentation to executives. The slides are ready. Your stomach is not.

outcomes.shine: You deliver it like a seasoned actor. Someone applauds, which is not allowed.
outcomes.flop: A slide shows the wrong chart. You say 'as you can see' to a blank screen.

wk_reply_all.text: You hit 'Reply All' with a message about the CEO's shoes. It was meant for one person.

outcomes.saved: The recall works. Mostly. Several people mention it kindly for years.
outcomes.too_late: The CEO answers three minutes later: 'They're comfortable.' You think about moving countries.

wk_remote_day.text: You're working from home. Your pajamas hold a meeting with your dignity.

outcomes.rested: The nap is perfect. Your afternoon output surprises everyone.
outcomes.missed: You wake up forty minutes into a call about you.

wk_client_nightmare.text: A client calls with seventeen urgent requests, three contradictory, one invented.

outcomes.respected: The client respects clarity, or at least pretends to. You've found a loophole in sanity.
outcomes.dropped: The client escalates to your boss. You look briefly like a villain in an email.

wk_secret_santa.text: Secret Santa. You drew the person who is allergic to everything and complains about it.

wk_sick_day.text: You wake up feeling decidedly gloomy. The inbox is full. Your lungs have opinions.

outcomes.fine: You're pale and productive. A coworker leaves soup on your desk anonymously.
outcomes.worse: You spread it to half the office. They remember.

wk_mentor.text: A senior colleague offers to mentor you. They mention 'brown-bag lunches' with an unsettling enthusiasm.

wk_expense_report.text: You find a $40 dinner receipt that doesn't belong to any work event. It would fit nicely into your expense report.

outcomes.slip: Nobody notices. You sleep fine and then don't.
outcomes.audit: An audit spots it. You get a stern email with 'integrity' in it.

wk_reorg.text: A reorganization is announced. A new chart replaces the old one. Your boxes have moved.

outcomes.new_team: You land on a team that actually likes meetings with agendas. Bliss.
outcomes.stuck: The transfer is declined, but they like your initiative. Somehow that's the worst news.

wk_performance_review.text: Your annual performance review arrives. Your manager uses the phrase 'room to grow' with great confidence.

outcomes.adjust: Your manager revises your score upward and avoids eye contact.
outcomes.no_change: Your manager notes your defensiveness as a development area.

wk_side_hustle.text: A friend proposes a side hustle selling hand-painted rocks online. It's weird. It might work.

outcomes.sells: The rocks sell. A man in another state buys forty. You don't ask.
outcomes.flop: You now own about two hundred painted rocks.

wk_gossip.text: You overhear something juicy about a manager's weekend. It involves a tuba. You should probably not repeat it.

outcomes.spreads: By noon the entire building knows about the tuba. The manager glares at you, correctly.
outcomes.quiet: Miraculously, it stays between you two. You will treasure it forever.

wk_deadline.text: The deadline is tomorrow. The project is a cathedral of loose ends.

outcomes.delivered: You deliver at dawn, wrinkled and victorious. Your boss calls it 'good hustle'.
outcomes.buggy: You deliver at dawn. Three people notice the mistakes by nine.

wk_inventory_theft.text: You see a coworker slipping a box of supplies into their bag. They notice you notice.

outcomes.handled: Management quietly handles it. The coworker leaves. No one thanks you, which is fair.
outcomes.backlash: Colleagues call you a snitch. You wear the title and a faint sense of rightness.

wk_fire_drill.text: The fire drill sounds mid-meeting. Everyone files out slowly, clutching laptops like newborns.
